requirement:
Give `read_node` the ID of a node. The result contains the node’s text. If more
text remains, pass `next` to `get_next_page`.

```text
read_node({node: NodeId}) -> {text: string, next?: UUID}
```
rationale:
The `read_node.mcp` text sets four obligations. The tool takes `{node: NodeId}`. The result carries `text`. The result carries `next` (a UUID) only when more text remains. That `next` is passed to `get_next_page`. The reviewed tests cover each one.

- **Complete read, no continuation.** `a_complete_node_read_has_text_and_no_continuation` calls `read_node` with `{"node":1}` on a short node. It asserts that the tool result content equals exactly `{"text":"short text"}`. That shows `text` is present and `next` is absent when nothing remains.
- **Truncated read with `next`.** `application_tools_preserve_graph_tools_in_the_same_conversation` reads an 18,000-character node. It asserts that the first result is `{"text": <8192 chars>, "next": <UUID>}`. The `next` value equals the one `returned_node_page` extracted from the `read_node` result. That helper parses `next` with `uuid::Uuid::parse_str`, so the value is checked to be a UUID. The test also asserts that every tool result is not an error.
- **Continuation via `get_next_page`.** In the same test, the scripted provider (`Script::complete` in `impl[Script/CompletionProvider]`) turns `use_next` into a `get_next_page` call. It takes the `uuid` argument from the `next` of the earlier `read_node` result. The follow-up page's `text` is asserted, and its own `next` is checked as a new, different UUID. So the returned `next` really is usable with `get_next_page` and yields more text.
- **Pagination retains the full text.** `graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change` uses multi-byte text that spans two pages. It checks that `next` is present on the first page only. It also checks that the concatenated page texts equal the original, even after the underlying contents change.
- **Input shape.** All of these tests call `read_node` with `{"node": <id>}` and the call succeeds. The first test also asserts that `read_node` is registered among the tools.

I found no input class, boundary or failure case in the text that lacks an asserting test.
